newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - UK traders prepare for share price falls.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - UK traders prepare for share price falls.

text.p: A number UK stock options were active on Thursday as traders took positions, fearing the underlying stocks would fall in the weeks ahead, dealers said.
The main deal in pharmaceuticals group SmithKline Beecham was a bear spread established by selling 1,075 July 900 calls at 175p and buying 1,075 July 1000 calls at 82p for a net credit of 93p.
At expiry, the deal will make a maximum profit of 93p if the underlying shares go below 900p.
SmithKline Beecham shares closed up 16-1/2p to 1092-1/2p.
There was also a bear spread in Cable & Wireless.
The deal involved selling 750 July 500 calls at 72p as well as buying 750 July 550 calls at 30p which will make a maximum 42p profit at expiry if the shares fall below 500p.
Shares in the telecomms group were down 7p to 570-1/2p.

Elsewhere, there was mixed trading in satellite television broadcaster British Sky Broadcasting where one trader -- possibly fearing the shares to drop -- bought 700 March 460 puts at 41p as well as BSkyB shares at 471p.
If the shares fall substantially, profits from the puts should offset losses from the shareholding. But if the shares rise, the cost of the puts will reduce the overall profit.
BSkyB shares ended the day down 14-1/2p to 456-1/2p.
Over in FTSE 100 index options, the bulk of deals were volatility trades in which an options position is hedged by an opposite position in FTSE futures.
One exception to this was a very bearish trade in which 5,000 July 4200 puts were bought at 5p in FTSE which will make money if the FTSE futures take a dive.
Cash FTSE closed up 17.9 at 4657.9 and September futures were up 24 at 4688.
